evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking API changes. The version string in backend_versions.json is an internal configuration detail that controls which backend binary version Lemonade requests; it does not alter any public API, CLI contract, or documented behavior. Upgrading from v1.0.3 to v1.0.4 is a transparent patch-level bump.
evidence.documentation: No documentation changes are required. This is a backend version bump that does not change user-facing behavior, CLI commands, API endpoints, or configuration options. Documentation updates would only be needed if the version change introduced new behavior or features that warrant explanation, which is not indicated here.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No to-do required. The change only modifies a version string in backend_versions.json. The FLM backend exists and is a shipped artifact on NPU, but this is a standard upstream version bump without code changes. The version will be downloaded at runtime when users request the FLM backend. Since the backend code path is unchanged and CI validated the full build and integration smoke tests, no manual exercise of the FLM endpoint is needed for this release. Residual risk: if FLM v1.0.4 has a bug not caught by upstream, it would surface at runtime on NPU hardware.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. The PR contains a single commit (72bac173f0507a204a138ccbe916b4de0a81d54d) authored by zaneni6 on 2026-09-01. The first and latest approvals were from @superm1 at 2026-09-02T04:25:25Z on the same commit. No commits were added after approval.
evidence.review: PR #3482 received an APPROVED review from @superm1 (superm1) on 2026-09-02T04:25:25Z. @superm1 has subject-matter expertise in FastFlowLM and NPU per docs/dev/contribute.md. There were no inline review comments and no additional comments on the PR. The PR was merged via merge group after all CI passed. The review was substantive enough for a trivial config change.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change only modifies a version number in a JSON resource file. No new dependencies, network calls, credential handling, or code execution paths are introduced. The backend binary itself is fetched from upstream at runtime, as always.
evidence.tests: No new tests were added, which is appropriate for a one-line JSON version number change. The full CI pipeline passed: C++ Server Build, Test, and Release (all platforms including ARM64), MCP Smoke Test, Docker Build Smoke Test, and all other workflows succeeded. The change is a config version bump that does not affect code logic and would not benefit from a dedicated unit test.
